steps.name: Senior Agent
steps.text: Report.

steps.name: Agent
steps.text: All pods on the levitation layer are now connected to the detonation web. We have people on the lower levels evacuating people from the square.

steps.name: Agent
steps.text: People are very passionate about the exhibition. Things will take some time, but it will not delay our plans.

steps.name: Agent
steps.text: We will detonate the levitation layer as soon as Propeller Paradise docks with the District.

steps.name: Senior Agent
steps.text: Any movement from Rhine?

steps.name: Agent
steps.text: We've taken twenty-three into custody. A dozen are still at large on the platforms.

steps.name: Agent
steps.text: We have control of the eight observation points. Those people are going in and out of the exhibit area and the ropeway stations. No special Rhine equipment other than standard maintenance gear.

steps.name: Senior Agent
steps.text: They're just playing hide-and-seek? No plan B?

steps.name: Senior Agent
steps.text: Keep an eye on them. They don't know the details of Maylander's plan, nor do they have any means of communication. Any last-gasp effort is doomed to fail.

steps.name: Agent
steps.text: Understood.
The outline of Max, D.C.—the most vibrant nomadic city in Columbia—is already visible from the ropeway station's waiting area.
The agents have not had a chance to enjoy the view of Propeller Paradise until now. With an excellent visibility, all the elaborate facilities of the levitation layer are brimming with vitality.
Pods float in mid-air like aquatic creatures. Floating botanical units line up orderly between small platforms, forming a power grid that supports the entire layer...

steps.name: Senior Agent
steps.text: Wait... where did you say Rhine's people were?

steps.name: Agent
steps.text: Exhibit area and ropeway stations.

steps.name: Senior Agent
steps.text: Where exactly? Show me.

steps.name: Senior Agent
steps.text: Looking at their movements, there's no way they can reach the platform where that 'tree' is, or other companies' pods...

steps.name: Senior Agent
steps.text: Could it be... they're not trying to take back their turf at all?

steps.name: Senior Agent
steps.text: But Rhine's people, the testers, and the company reps, they all seem to be flying around blindly in the dark...

steps.name: Senior Agent
steps.text: What's the point of it all?
The agent casts a casual glance at the nearest planting unit. The unremarkable Rhine creation stands quietly.
He suddenly realizes that the warning lights on their edges are easily visible even during the day, and they have been blinking irregularly for quite a while now.

steps.name: Agent
steps.text: Spotters report that all the Rhine people have disappeared from sight!

steps.name: Senior Agent
steps.text: No, they didn't disappear!

steps.name: Senior Agent
steps.text: They're going in the same direction... there's a pattern to their movement!

steps.name: Senior Agent
steps.text: Everybody, listen up! Destroy all the planting units you see along the way! They're not decorations! Rhine is using them to communicate!

steps.name: Senior Agent
steps.text: Cut off the exhibit area from all the ropeway stations, and find every one of those people playing hide-and-seek! Find out where they're heading!

steps.name: Senior Agent
steps.text: What on Terra are they thinking...

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: You've been looking outside the window for a while.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: You said you must win your gamble, and you have a reason.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: I'm in the middle of a gamble too.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: I have a rough idea what's going on in Propeller Paradise, given the look on your face and the freefall that we just experienced.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: You wouldn't run this kind of risk with me for no reason. But there's nothing I can offer you now, except—

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: You want the Lucky Cystybeast?

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: You could say that.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: I want the contraband that Gordon Tannen sold you.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Coming to the broadcast room to bother me, when you should be preparing your own speech? You sure have a thick hide, Mr. Tannen.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I would have died a long time ago if all my enemies refused to work with me ever again.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Work with you? I'm afraid I can't.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Maylander has a laundry list of violations that I committed during my career. I don't want to spend the rest of my days giving prison tours.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Neither are you looking for a peaceful life. Besides, my proposal has something to do with Maylander.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: There's no better vantage point than here on Propeller Paradise. Oakley's too excited to notice, but I doubt you would miss what's going on.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Well, if I gotta say it...

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: The broadcast screens of the levitation layer are switching too quickly. They say it's because they're doing testing, which I'm not convinced about. There are a dozen testers on the square whom I don't recognize. They don't look like they're taking a stroll; they look like they're patrolling.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Like they know that danger is impending.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Are you trying to trick me into another plot?

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: There's a plot afoot on Propeller Paradise alright, that's a fact. It's also a fact that I won't let Gustave make a mockery out of this place in front of all of Columbia.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: You have ten seconds. Yes or no.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: What are the chances of success?

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Ten percent.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Doesn't sound like a gamble you'd take.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I don't have a choice with that old fox sitting across the table, holding all the cards.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: A plan almost certain to fail... interesting. Tell me about it.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I need you to convince as many people as possible to return to the levitation layer, and retrieve the Originium equipment and Arts units on this list.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: ...All contraband that you sold?

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: They have far more potential than just sitting under the spotlight.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: You want to...

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Escape. And take all of Propeller Paradise with me.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Gustave and Maylander never intended to allow the exhibition to go ahead. The opening ceremony was just a smokescreen.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: The levitation layer will fall a second time soon. But miracles don't happen a second time.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: The Lucky Cystybeast can't afford to start over...

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Neither can most startups on Propeller Paradise.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: 'Escape. And take all of Propeller Paradise...'

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: It's the only way to save both Propeller Paradise and the people on the lower level.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Propeller Paradise has been traveling on the barrenlands for seven days. Fuel is short, and the plate is operating in safe mode. The basic propulsion module is not enough to change its direction.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: But the Arts unit that the Lucky Cystybeast got was just a transformation stabilizer. It can't supply enough energy to turn a plate.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Correct.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: But it wasn't the only item that Tannen smuggled.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: You mean, get all the contraband devices, and build a makeshift propulsion module to make the plate deviate from its course?

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Not deviate. Make an about-face.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: About-face? Have you any idea what you're saying? It's the direction of the borders!

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: True, the procedures for cross-border travel is a little complicated.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: It would be treason!

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: No, I can't go to jail. People need to see Lucky Cystybeast on the broadcasts. My wife in Northville needs to see it...

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: In the interest of full disclosure, I must inform you that people won't see Lucky Cystybeast on the broadcasts, whether we succeed or fail.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: No...

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: I'm sorry, but I'm taking the unit, whether you give it up voluntarily or not. We don't have time.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: What's the point? We can't even leave the pod...

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Someone has unlocked it remotely.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: You see the floating botanical units outside the window? Three flashes is a distress call. The current message is cycled after five continuous seconds of being lit.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Right now... three, four, five... seven flashes.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Looks like the other units on the list have been retrieved. Everyone is rendezvousing on Platform 7. Wait—

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: ...The light went out.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: What does that mean?

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: It means Maylander knows what's up. We're in danger.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Mr. Aspen, you can either come with me on your feet, or you can go to sleep right here, right now.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: People like us never get to choose, do we?

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: Sit down.
Gustave looks at the Savra who has butted heads with him for seven years, who now sits stiffly on a chair, like a potato wrapped in foil.
He knows young officers well. They are angry, flamboyant, unhappy about everything, and frustrated about being restricted by rules.
In the end, however, they all sit in the same chair that rectifies their young spine, and become a proper member of the upper stratum of Columbian society.
As Gordon Tannen will.

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: Once Maylander's plan succeeds, the broadcast room will switch over to Cloud. Don't screw up.

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: Put your usual attitude away. Sound sincere, devastated. It's the Propeller Paradise you built. It won't be hard to stir the appropriate emotions.

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: Tomorrow, that sorry face of yours is going to be on the front page of every Columbian newspaper. Look the part, won't you?

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: And stop staring at your little freak.

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: I know, I know. You don't want to be Propeller Paradise's sin eater, sharing the same spotlight as Nasti.

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: But your little hotchpotch trinket isn't going to save you.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: So I'm sitting in Gordon Tannen's defendant seat.

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I can follow you to the DOD once I apologize, according to the script?

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: Do as you're told, and you'll rise quickly through the ranks.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Yeah, guess what? I don't give a shit.

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: What was that?

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I don't like this seat. It makes my scales itch.

steps.name: Communicator
steps.text: ...Broadcast countdown. Cloud restaurant, stand by...

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: Broadcast? Now?

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: Impossible... no movement on the levitation layer. Did Maylander screw up?

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: Who's operating the broadcast?!

steps.name: Communicator
steps.text: Three, two, one—

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Do it, Five-Four.

steps.name: Space Finbeast
steps.text: Yes, sir!

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: Ugh—
As the broadcast cuts to the Cloud restaurant, Space Fin 054 leaps at an unprepared Gustave, pinning him to the ground.
The screen in the restaurant lights up, and Gustave sees his own face, writhing in pain and shock.
He knows that this face is being displayed on every screen in Propeller Paradise.

His contingency plans flash before his eyes, but Maylander's plan is in its final phase, leaving little room for distractions. His communicator lies in pieces on the ground, destroyed by Space Fin 054.
Gordon stretches his neck and wrists, crushes the 'defendant seat' with his foot, and leisurely lies down on the sofa next to it.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Oh, that felt good—

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: By the way, tomorrow, that sorry face of yours is gonna be on the front page of every Columbian newspaper. Look the part, won't you?

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: You—

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: What, you didn't expect to be immobilized by a little 'hobby made to fuel sky fever'?

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: You're the elder statesman of ATAO, planning a new chapter at the Department of Defense. You made the rules of Columbia when you were young, and you continue to 'serve your country' even after your retirement...

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Woo-hoo. First-rate, ain't you? Maybe you've grown into thinking that your enemies will always use the rules to fight back, in smart and clever ways.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Did you forget that Gordon Tannen is a bandit who never gives a shit about the rules, a piece of trash obsessed with his toys?

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I guess I shouldn't be surprised. You don't even recognize Five-Four, even though I didn't change its voice module—

steps.name: Space Finbeast
steps.text: Hello, Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Arts Units, and Originium, at your service. To check the progress of an application, press 1. To report a safety risk, press 2. To be connected to an operator, press 0...

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: ...An ATAO answering machine?

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I said Space Fin 054 wasn't a rich man's cigar. And I won't be smug just because it obeys the rules I set down.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Seven years ago, I sat on a tiny chair that made my ass hurt, writing my first self-reflection letter late at night, wondering if I should quit.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Answering Machine 054 started giving off an unusual noise, and I racked my brains trying to figure out the problem.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I started studying every Arts unit and Originium device that passed through my hands, just to give Five-Four the ability to operate, communicate, and think on its own.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: You think the hundreds of self-reflection letters I wrote were the symbol of my submission. But Five-Four is the real culmination of my seven years at ATAO!

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: You're full of crap! You didn't learn the tricks of bureaucracy for your little invention!

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: You think I've never seen you negotiate or threaten? Arrogant, vain, ambitious... I know them when I see it.

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: I can hear shadows of my own speeches even now as you're talking to me.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: ...I never thought I was perfect.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Maybe I will never be able to get rid of the bad habits that I learned from you. They disgust me, but they weren't mistakes.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: My only mistake was to define my transactions as 'smuggling'. I shouldn't have allowed myself to accept the rules that have taken form, rules that don't make sense.

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: Foolish boy, you don't understand what's at stake—

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Listen, old slug.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I don't care what high-and-mighty reasons you have. Propeller Paradise isn't supposed to be a breeding ground of war.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Sure, kinetic engines and high-powered Arts unit could become powerful weapons, but what they're supporting now is the dream of life in the sky.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Until Propeller Paradise docks with the District, I'm its chief executive, the man who built this little piece of heaven that still has a semblance of freedom—

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I will decide whether it should be destroyed, or whether it should escape.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Take his passcode, Five-Four.

steps.name: Space Finbeast
steps.text: Yes, sir.

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: It's no use. The central control console is locked. You can't stop the plate from docking with the District, even if you have my passcode.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Who said anything about stopping?

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: What...?

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I said, 'escape'.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Not only did the former head of ATAO not disable his passcode when he retired, he used the security access it granted to disable the urban identification code system on the Columbian border...

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Cool, isn't it?

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: You're going to commit treason for this stupid, pointless children's playground?

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: Hah. You were right. You didn't learn a single thing from me.

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: Let me remind you that Propeller Paradise is running out of fuel. You can't operate the plate's steering system, and you don't have enough energy.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Even when you're pinned to the ground by the robot I built, you somehow manage to forget that I've always been an inventor.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I hope they deliver the goods on time.
The sound of rotary motors has never been so clear.
The skies are clear. Overly-pristine self-cleaning artificial clouds combine with natural clouds to form a wondrous scene, but the people on the platforms are oblivious to it.
Some fifty Propeller Paradise guards and Maylander agents block off every passage and cable connections, forming an impregnable cordon line with their bodies and weapons.
Beneath their feet, the classical black-and-white tiles form a chessboard, the two sides separated by a ten-meter-long open-air passage.
The eyes of the agents are fixed on the support platform on the other side of the passage. The Rhine staff and testers who had at one point disappeared from sight now assemble there.

steps.name: Agent A
steps.text: Platform 7... the analysis was correct. This is where the hide-and-seek converges.

steps.name: Agent A
steps.text: Our people are ready, but there are more of them than expected.

steps.name: Agent B
steps.text: They took out our guys in the broadcast room. The intel was not accurate.

steps.name: Agent B
steps.text: We're putting in everyone we have.

steps.name: Agent A
steps.text: Strength in numbers alone isn't enough. Be on your guard. They have an advantage when it comes to the new weapons and lay of the land.

steps.name: Agent A
steps.text: Propeller Paradise is about to dock with D.C. Do not let anyone pass.

steps.name: Agent A
steps.text: Use force if necessary. I'll take responsibility.

steps.name: Agent B
steps.text: Yes, sir.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: Six elite squads...

steps.name: Tester
steps.text: We have numbers, but the guys on the other side are...

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: Hard to tell people to keep going when they're exhausted.

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: Get the word out to the others, Jelena. Anyone who's too tired to move, give someone else their core components, pick up any hover unit, and stay behind to guard the support platform.

steps.name: Tester
steps.text: You're betting on them being wary about unknown new products?

steps.name: Sky Jagger
steps.text: I hope it works.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Phew... made it.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: Are you sure you want to go this way when it's like this?

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Yes, this is the only way to Cloud.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Take my parachute. Things might get dangerous.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: What about you?

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Me?
Ferne gazes at the Maylander blockade with interest, as though she is going to meet an old rival.
The camera drones left Platform 7 half an hour ago. Nothing that is about to happen here will be seen in the broadcast room.
Everyone knows that conflict is inevitable. Neither side wants to delay.
Their eyes are fixed on each other. Everyone is waiting for a sign.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: My tour is waiting for my signal.
Suddenly, a yellow-and-black warning flag is raised. A young Feline woman leaps out from the crowd, loudspeaker in hand.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: The first day I snuck onto Propeller Paradise, a kind guide told me that no one in this place can be stopped, if even the sky is no longer off-limits.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: From the exhibits to the underground lab, I memorized every strange and curious invention, the complex ideas behind them, and hundreds of thousands of words of descriptions.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: I could tell you who made the flying toaster above our heads, its model, and the generation.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: I could go on and on about how wonderful they are, but to be completely honest, I find the levitating plates less interesting than the sunset of Bleached Wasteland.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Then I remember what my father used to say to me: 'A story is always more interesting than an explanation.'

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: I've had many frustrating experiences in the years that I worked as an independent guide.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: There's nothing wrong with seeking truth, but many people subconsciously disparage exaggeration, inspiration, and dreams yet to come true.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: I swore I would never again label things that I've never seen for myself as 'impossible', and laugh at my own family with my neighbors, as I did I few years ago—

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: It was not until the day my father died that I truly understood what he said.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: If Propeller Paradise needed a guide, I would rather tell the people of Columbia about the people I met here, about their stories.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Rice Bush.

steps.name: Lively Tester
steps.text: H-Huh?

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: A cobbler from Bunkerhill whose dream was to leave a footprint on each of the twin moons, so that everyone who looks up with a telescope would see his shop's logo on the shoeprints.

steps.name: Lively Tester
steps.text: There's no bigger billboard than the sky, after all...

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Owen Fredericks.

steps.name: Calm Tester
steps.text: ...I'm here.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Hardware store owner who wants to put his own screw on the second Ring Lab, and earn a spot for his family when space colonization becomes reality.

steps.name: Calm Tester
steps.text: Hey, never hurts to be prepared for the future.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Aspen—

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: I'll tell it myself.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: Aspen, grocer from Northville.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: After being tricked into taking out exploitative loans, I divorced my wife and left home, so the creditors wouldn't go after my family.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: My wife and I came up with the name 'Lucky Cystybeast' together. We haven't spoken to each other in two years.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: She was worried sick when I left. I promised that the name 'Lucky Cystybeast' would be on TV, so that she'd know I'm safe.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: Now I know that the exhibition was one big, fat lie. But I want her to at least see this red balloon with the Lucky Cystybeast logo on it, even if all the pods crash.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Aspen, and all of you.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: The things we want, whether they're based in reality or just a pipe dream, whether they're the result of blind conformity or superstition... they're much more important than Maylander and Gustave think they are.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Run! Jump! Fly!

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: We'll overcome everything that tries to block our path and change us, without ever trying to understand us. We're the ones who'll decide Propeller Paradise's path!
Ferne dashes forward like a fowlbeast, loudly blasting her signal, as the rest of the pack follows behind, charging at the Maylander blockade.
Exhibits fly over the heads of the pushing and squeezing crowd, carrying all kinds of contraband towards the sky.
Absurd, and flying free.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Phew... finally out of the woods. Good work, guys. We just have to hang in there a little longer.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Thirty-four contraband core components.... all intact. Looks like the landing module works quite well.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: My work is almost done. All that's left is to deliver this to Gordon. Hope all is well on his side.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Next—
Put it down.
Turn around.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Y-You're Gustave's science consultant? What are you doing here...?
Outside the window, the pinnacle of the D.C. Government Office and the Columbian flag are already visible.
Gordon's eyes are fixed on the bottom-left of the broadcast, as the red dot on the map gets closer and closer to the District plate.
According to the plan, the devices on the list should have been delivered to Cloud more than ten minutes ago.
He forces himself to not look at the door. Gustave is bound to notice any sign of anxiety.

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: The plan isn't going the way you expected it, is it?

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: You're calmer than I expected.

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: Being willing to take risks is not a bad thing, but you're not good enough at assessing risk.

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: You didn't have time to prepare a Plan B for your reckless Plan A. All of you will pay a heavy price if it fails.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: And what's YOUR Plan B?

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: It's all good and well to rediscover your confidence, but never forget who you're competing with. I told you that getting carried away will cause you to overlook fatal flaws.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: What do you mean...?

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: You're late.

steps.name: Scientific Consultant
steps.text: I was delayed.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Your science consultant...

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: More than just a science consultant. I needed insurance for my plan.
The tall, dark Kuranta walks towards Gordon. The box holding thirty-four Originium devices, safely contained by protective material, seems almost weightless in his hands.
He lifts his arm and hands the box over to Gordon.

steps.name: Scientific Consultant
steps.text: What you wanted.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Thanks.

steps.name: Gustave
steps.text: What are you doing?

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I learned a lot from you. Of course I knew what your trump card was.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: A rival to provoke competition. A scientific consultant with both brains and brawn. A fair and impartial outsider to give legitimacy to the hearing and plan.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Too bad you picked the wrong guy.

steps.name: Scientific Consultant
steps.text: Gramophone made from the tentacles of fossilized Seaborn? Decorative, or specifically functional?

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Oh, it's for—

steps.name: Scientific Consultant
steps.text: I see, automatic tuning with the Seaborn's sound-producing structures...

steps.name: Scientific Consultant
steps.text: The grooves on the edge indicate that the designer even tested whether Seaborn adjust their biostructure based on the music. An interesting idea.

steps.name: Scientific Consultant
steps.text: Where does this golden skeletal hand come from?

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: The one on the wall is from Sar—

steps.name: Scientific Consultant
steps.text: It forms a pair with the heavily corroded one on the shelf, doesn't it?

steps.name: Scientific Consultant
steps.text: The construction of the joints and the level of wear-and-tear indicates that it originated from the western deserts of Sargon.

steps.name: Scientific Consultant
steps.text: Ah, this runed dagger is a familiar face. It—

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: They were supposed to be a pair!

spans.text: were supposed to be a pair!

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I got it from a Sami snowpriest, who said a pair of lovers put a curse on it with their blood. It's driven by witchcraft, and cuts through iron like butter...

steps.name: Scientific Consultant
steps.text: I know. The other one was once impaled in my heart.

steps.name: Scientific Consultant
steps.text: It no longer cuts through iron like butter, but it's still good enough to carve a walking stick.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Mr. Consultant, I apologize for any offense I might have caused, and I understand your desire for recompense.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: But I don't have time. I brought you here for a serious purpose.

steps.name: Scientific Consultant
steps.text: If we take off part of the structure of the gramophone and combine it with the sensor module on the metal skeletal hand, we might create a new type of voice-guided navigation model.

steps.name: Scientific Consultant
steps.text: That witchcraft-driven blade can serve as a low-loss needle. And here, this high-powered Originium internal combustion engine, legal only in Rim Billiton, can provide thirty times the power of standard Columbian equipment.

steps.name: Scientific Consultant
steps.text: If only we can find a Victorian transformation stabilizer, which is no longer in production, and a Locus of Sorcery that was once seen on the Columbian barrenlands—

steps.name: Scientific Consultant
steps.text: We'd almost have all the parts necessary to put together the initial core assembly of a nomadic plate's mobility layer.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: You know what I'm planning to do?

steps.name: Scientific Consultant
steps.text: Trying to modify an entire plate's power source with a single device is extremely risky, but not impossible.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: You're not one of Gustave's guys. Who are you?

steps.name: Scientific Consultant
steps.text: You're the one who said you don't have time.

steps.name: Scientific Consultant
steps.text: The real question is, what do you need me to do?
Gordon glares at the Kuranta standing at the center of the collection room.
The Kuranta recognized all Gordon's collections, saw through all Gordon's thoughts, and nonchalantly revealed a glimpse into his own past, as though he had pursued death across the land...
To Gordon, the Kuranta seems to stroll through the halls of his thoughts, like a king that knows nothing, and everything.
Once again, the spikes on the Savra's tail rise up on their ends, swaying conspicuously.
This time, it is not because he is on guard, but because of the excitement of victory being in sight.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: How's the stability of the power unit?

steps.name: Scientific Consultant
steps.text: It will last no more than three days, or one day and a half, if fuel is insufficient.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Good enough.

steps.name: Scientific Consultant
steps.text: You don't actually plan on driving it out of Columbia.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: You don't think I would shit on everyone's future for a grudge?

steps.name: Scientific Consultant
steps.text: That's what you want people to think, to allow you to protect as many people as possible.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Is that so?

steps.name: Scientific Consultant
steps.text: Treason is a serious crime.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Pfft, you should look up my file. I've got enough charges against me as it is.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Come, help me take these stuff to the control room.

The wings of a fowlbeast, the horn of a burdenbeast, the teeth of a manglerbeast, the hide of a sandbeast, and the blood of a beckbeast. What would happen if you took something from thirty-four creatures and put it all together?
Sharp, weird, chaotic, dangerous, malicious... these are the thoughts that flash through Gordon's mind as he gazes upon the power unit he just created.
But he is also filled with excitement that threatens to drive him mad.

steps.name: Scientific Consultant
steps.text: The plate's original power system has been turned off. The device is now connected.

steps.name: Scientific Consultant
steps.text: You may now decide the course of Propeller Paradise.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I swore an oath when I got my transfer notice.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I would be the one who lights the fire of everything new on Propeller Paradise.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: I would do everything I can to make even the stupidest ideas come true. No one would ever again feel the pain I felt at ATAO, to be forced to admit their own uselessness in rules set by others.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Now, I'm still the one who lights the fire, except I'm doing it to the engine of Propeller Paradise, and let it run into the empty wilderness.
Gordon grabs the fierce-looking lever on the power unit and takes a deep breath.

steps.name: Gordon
steps.text: Say goodbye to Max, D.C., Propeller Paradise.

steps.name: Agent
steps.text: Tin Man, that Ferne is leading a group on Platform 7...

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: ...I see it through the monitors.

steps.name: Agent
steps.text: Looks like Tannen got one up on Gustave at Cloud.

steps.name: Agent
steps.text: Hearing from the guys monitoring the Rhine tree. Nasti has broke through the blockade. Our guys are trying to follow her, but they're being blocked by something that feels like Sarkaz witchcraft.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Væla...

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Send a team over and get the situation under control. I'll deal with matters on the Rhine side.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Looks like we're going to meet an old friend, Larry, Curly and Mo... a mad Banshee on the brink of death might be a bit of a headache to deal with.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: As for you, Merry, you can choose to stay here, or help our colleagues outside.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: You should stay a little longer.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Hey, you three...
Tin Man hears no answer from his revenant friends.
Ol' Curly is lithely waving a stick and dancing an impromptu tap dance. Big Larry lies on top of Mercia's head with tears in his eyes, recalling memories of who-knows-what. As for Lil' Mo...
He is howling and yelling, and Tin Man can hear—
He seems to think he is back in Kazdel, taking out a revolver and emptying it into the elder revenant trying to stuff him into the furnace.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: My legs are numb, and I'm a little dizzy...

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: Perhaps you've been lax about your exoskeleton maintenance.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: This brain isn't supposed to rust.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Your Arts have improved considerably, huh? You managed to drag these three into the whirlpool of memory, even though Ol' Curly had confiscated the projector.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: Or was it dumb luck? Did all the memories of their overly long lives make it easier for you to manipulate?

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: It will take a long time to play through the movies of your lives, even at 320x speed, not to mention all the moments that need to be paused and replayed...

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: I apologize.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: You understand that the effectiveness against me is limited.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: Yes, I'm sure you'll break free of the shackles quite soon. I've read the Ho'olheyak reports... she could not fully incapacitate you, even after lopping your head off.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: Therefore, all I can do is stall for as much time as possible, and delay your intervention.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: You're an outstanding agent, Merry.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: You've always been doing an admirable job, helping people forget what they should, be it through Arts or other means.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: But this is the wrong time, and you've chosen the wrong target.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: You told me not to forget my family name... I've never forgotten.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: Any Selene who grew up in that old house would never forget.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: The 'orphanage' of Maylander Selene, predecessor of the Foundation.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: It was our 'home'. We truly considered Mr. Selene our grandfather when we were little.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: Do you know what my most vivid memory of him is?

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: When I was eight, I came home from school one day to find the doll, that should have been in my room, spinning in the middle of the garden, watering the grass around it.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: It was the only thing I had that reminded me of my mother. I don't remember her face, but I remember her thimbles gleaming under the lamp when she sewed the doll for me.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: Grandpa turned it into a sprinkler without a single word to me, as though the doll was always meant to do that.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: The children who grew up with me all have similar stories.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: You were Grandpa's best friend. You know that, to the 'Founding Father of the Federation', there are only new things in Columbia, the youngest nation on Terra, rising out of the frontiers...

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: The only reason for old things to stay is to be used for pioneering.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: It didn't matter if we were Victorian emigrants or Gaulish refugees, whether we were children of debtors or criminals.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: Grandpa wanted us to become the children of Columbia, become Selenes. That was the only reason for our existence.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: However, that's exactly why I can't accept what's happening right now, and take it for granted.

steps.name: Tin Man
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: I can't begin to imagine what you experienced in the long course of history. The Maylander Foundation, the president, the vice-president, they all have more things to think about...

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: I've seen the analyses on Kazimierzian power armor. They've reverse-engineered the technology of the Gaulish Vieux Vanguard, achieving results that surpassed the 'Transmitter' using the flesh and blood of knights.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: I've read the textbooks of Leithanian 'Basic Arts Tactics' courses. It will not be a surprise if, in a decade, every citizen of Leithanien is a soldier, as is the case for Laterano.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: I can understand why Maylander thinks Columbia is falling behind, and how a timely arms race could bring us back on the 'right track'.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: Judging by the standards that Grandpa taught me so many times, there is nothing more efficient from the perspective of national development.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: It's not that I don't understand these fallacies. Indeed, if I was asked to deal with these problems, I would draw a blank, and I would be able to do little else but cry.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: But I just can't take it for granted. Not now.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: If orphans like us, who had nowhere to go, could all become children of Columbia—

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: Then why should a mother who walked a thousand miles in search of her daughter, a merchant who put everything on the line so that his wife would not be hounded by creditors, and testers who are simply trying to earn a living...

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: Why should they be sacrificed for the sake of Columbia's progress?

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: My job is to make people forget. But this time...

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: You decided to pay a price for Columbia's progress. You shouldn't be allowed to forget. You should remember the lives and dreams that were part of the sacrifice.

steps.name: Mercia
steps.text: Don't think of it as no big deal.
Nasti gazes at the indistinct figure within the winding branches. The figure of her mother.
Væla's limbs have been replaced by grey-white branches, bark climbing up her clothes and skin like scales, printing countless indistinct visages.
Glowing resin pours down like a waterfall, obscuring her face. Many desperate hands reach out from within, clutching her throat like clutching at straws.
Both the 'tree' and the person within seem almost unrecognizable.
There is only one thing that Nasti can be sure of: this was not a natural occurrence.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: You merged with the tree?

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Falling... I see your road back falling, collapsing. I must make sure you can go home.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: My incantation could not reach the broken path, but the roots of this Roosting Tree will.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: ...I harmed it.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: (In Sarkaz) Unravel!
Nasti's incantation goes unanswered.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: The tree's design was based on the grammar of the Banshees. It remains flawed in many ways, but it has never before rejected my incantation. Yet now...
The branches continue to spread around Væla, dragging her floating silhouette towards Nasti, bit by bit.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Pease, Væla, stop... let me analyze what's happened to you.
Nasti's plea goes unanswered too.
All Væla does is ask questions, in an urgent, trembling voice.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: There's no mistapple pulp outside the valley... how do you polish your feather horns, Nasti?

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: I never taught you incantations, but it looks like you've learned it on your own... a kind of imitation... how did you...?

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: And your bone pen... your... your...

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: That's not important, Væla. What I need to know is what happened to you here.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Not... important?
Væla is suddenly silent, and the creeping branches come to a standstill.
An instant later, they start to spread in the opposite direction, encroaching upon what is left of Væla.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: The fusion is progressing?

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: This Roosting Tree has shared your memories with me... where you went... what you did...

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: It can share more... more important things.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: I saw you dig for answers in the great library of the Lich for days and nights... you ruined your eyesight, but the curmudgeon Fremont kicked you out in the end.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: I should have told him that you were never a foolish child. It was because of me...

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: I saw you bind your horns and attach fowlbeast feathers to them every day, just to sneak into the city of the Sankta to find food...

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: But it was bad for your horns. That's why the one on the right stopped growing, isn't it?

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: I saw you sleep on metal scaffolds, where there were no leaves to give you shade. You didn't built a treehouse either, just used a simple metal plate...

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: How could anyone sleep like that...? Do you get sick?
Nasti listens to her go on and on. The voice is distorted, barely recognizable, but the words of concern are familiar.
Væla used to say these things when they lived in Convallis.
Nasti realizes that she is not looking at a problem that needs to be solved, nor a patient who needs to be treated.
She is looking at a worried mother who needs to be understood.
Nasti lowers her bone pen.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Ferne told me how you looked like when she found you. There were burns from Arts, holes from bullets, and gashes from sandstorms all over you...

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: You walked the path that I once did, only harder and more painfully.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: You could have died... you should have stayed in the Convallis.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: There was nothing more I could do for the valley, for Laqeramaline, for the children.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: You've already done so much. The lies you weaved for the sake of all the Banshees...

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: I knew it... they couldn't fool you.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: I began to sense that something was off soon after you brought me to the Convallis.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: I've kept the lie going for two hundred years. This was my greatest achievement as custodian of the valley, and my greatest sin...

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Two hundred years... do you mean... that war?

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: The King of Sarkaz at the time was old and foolish. It was not just the Royal Courts; even outsiders thought they could turn him into a puppet and thus control all Sarkaz.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: It was already a bad year. Catastrophe raked the land once, then the alliance's guns raked it again.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: The green Feline appeared on the horizon, leading a wall of steel that stretched as far as the eye could see. Which were the Steam Knights, which were the spire casters, and which were the Vieux Vanguard? I couldn't tell.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: I don't know when they learned to build ships of steel, and tubes that breathed fire.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: All I remember is that the towering Wendigos could only whimper as they were crushed beneath the ships, and our kin fell burning from the sky like broken kites.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: No one who heard the wailing that day would ever forget it.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: ...The wailing of the Banshee.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: We couldn't tell if we were delivering death, or delivering the dead. All we could do was wail and howl, hardly able to put together a single coherent elegy.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: There were less than a thousand of us left when the allied forces withdrew from Kazdel. Half of us had lost our voices.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Because of our nature, the Banshees have never missed a single war of the Sarkaz. But such losses were unprecedented.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: I survived by sheer chance and left the blood-soaked land of sorrows, trying to find a place where life still remained.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: The Convallis?

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: The Convallis.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: The vast Mist Lake separates it from the outside. The seasons come to a still in the golden woods. It is a quiet place... one that seemed like it didn't belong to the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: There's nothing that shouldn't belong to Sarkaz.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Yes... we believed it at the time. Me, Laqeramaline, and the new king chosen by the crown.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: We believed in a new life for the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Laqeramaline and I took our remaining kin into the Convallis, built a dock by Mist Lake, and built our court in the forests.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: For the first time, we added symbols of life into the song of the Banshee, guided the trees to bear rich fruit, and the vines to weave themselves into bridges with incantations.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: For the first time, the Banshees settled in a single place. They no longer had to sleep with only the night sky as their blanket, traveling from one death to another.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: But 'tokens' from outside soon came flying in like snowflakes.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Tokens announcing death.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: ...Yes.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Not even Theresa and Theresis could solve the problems left behind by war overnight.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Yes. Death lingers, long after the smoke has cleared.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: We made dried fruit out of our first harvest. It was barely enough for a few hundred Banshees to make it through the coldest month of winter.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: But the tokens in my room... the murky blood crystals of the Vampires, tattered shrouds of the Nachzehrers, the shriveled, rosen hearts that Djaj become...

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: They soon piled higher, much higher than our dried fruit. I knew that if we went out to deliver the dead at that time...

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: We would return to our old path. But the catalyst for change was won with the lives of thousands upon thousands in war.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: So you made a choice on behalf of all the Banshees.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: I made the choice. I convinced Laqeramaline.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: I concealed all the tokens announcing death coming from outside.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Occasionally a Banshee might leave the Convallis to deliver our kin, but I chose the people carefully and sparingly... Laqeramaline faced much criticism outside.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: For a long time, we believed that we could cast aside our nature and lead a different life. If the Banshees could do it, so could all Sarkaz.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Even if the price was that the owners of the tokens would never find their way to the myriad souls.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Even the price was that the Banshees, having violated their nature, are swallowed by a lifetime of emptiness, destined to endure a long and painful journey of forgetting upon their deathbed.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Two hundred years passed. Two hundred years we had endured.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Until I met you.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: ...That's why I had to leave.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: How many deaths did you tell the others about each month? More people die in Kazdel every day.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: You could fool the others, but you knew that I knew from the beginning.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Laqeramaline was right. You were too smart, and you grew up in Kazdel... I could not have fooled you.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: But I hoped you could live in the Convallis.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Not just because your mother was one of the many thousands of souls that I turned a blind eye to... not just because I owed you a happy childhood for failing to respond to the last wish in time.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: But also because I hoped that the Convallis, the sanctuary that was built in the hope of seeking a new life for the Sarkaz, would at least be able to take in a child from outside after two hundred years.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: I took the child who was most likely to expose my lie in, as my daughter.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: You carefully kept me away from other Banshees.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Ultimately, your hopes for the Convallis fell through.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: I made many mistakes in my life. But there is none that I regret more than your departure.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: You were always a smart girl. I've thought about it many times... that if I had told you the truth about things, you would have understood and played along whatsoever.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: If that was the case, then perhaps you wouldn't have...

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: No, I would have left regardless.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: I remember the day we parted.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: You called out to me. I didn't turn around, but I looked down at the water.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: There was no wind on Mist Lake that day. The boat sailed across the water like a knife cutting through a piece of paper. I saw your face clearly, reflected in the still water.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: You wept when I said I was leaving, but let out a sigh of relief... so small, so imperceptible, that perhaps you didn't even notice it yourself.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Deep down, you wanted me to leave, didn't you?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: We were co-conspirators in the parting.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Haven't you realized it, Væla?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: It is the Convallis, not me, that is truly your daughter.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: You discovered it, entrusted the Sarkaz's future to it, and built it with pavilions and boats, fruits and cakes.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Your love for it grew as time passed.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: There were two reasons why you brought me back to the Convallis: to make amends for the price you paid for it, and to verify whether it has grown the way you hoped it would.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: My departure brought relief, because the one who could expose the fragile lie that ties the Convallis together left.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: But my departure also brought anguish, because it proved that the valley could not carry the burden you hoped it would, even after two hundred years.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: It was too fragile to accept a child who grew up in Kazdel, much less become the future abode of all Sarkaz.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Nasti, don't...

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Do you know the answer, Væla?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: You left the Convallis, came here, and merged with this tree, which is like the Roosting Tree, yet different... did you do it for me, for yourself, or simply out of obsession?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: What are you running from, Væla?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Are you running from death, from the failure of the Convallis, or from the fact that you are dying and there is nothing else you can do for the Convallis's failure?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Tell me, help me understand, and put an end to this error.
